{{Short description|American biologist and author}}'''Paul R. Gross''' is an American [[biologist]] and author, perhaps best known to the general public for ''[[Higher Superstition]]'' (1994), written with [[Norman Levitt]].<ref>{{Cite book |last=Rothenberg |first=Marc |title=Magill's Literary Annual 1995 |date=June 1995 |publisher=Salem Press |chapter=Higher Superstition |chapter-url=https://search.ebscohost.com/login.aspx?direct=true&db=lkh&AN=164501773&lang=en-gb&site=eds-live&scope=site |via=[[EBSCOhost]]}}</ref> Gross is the University Professor of Life Sciences (Emeritus) at the [[University of Virginia]];<ref>{{Cite web |date=January 4, 2000 |title=Paul R. Gross |url=https://search.ebscohost.com/login.aspx?direct=true&db=lkh&AN=49396645&lang=en-gb&site=eds-live&scope=site |access-date=2025-06-24 |website=Baker & Taylor Author Biographies |via=[[EBSCOhost]]}}</ref> he previously served the university as [[Provost (education)|Provost]] and vice-president.<ref name=":0">{{Cite web |title=Paul R. Gross, PhD, ScD, Fellow |url=https://www.scienceinmedicine.org/fellows/Gross.html |access-date=2025-06-24 |website=Institute for Science in Medicine}}</ref> He has written widely on the intellectual conflicts of the [[science wars]], [[biology]], [[evolution]], and [[creationism]]—for example, his book ''[[Creationism's Trojan Horse|Creationism's Trojan Horse: The Wedge of Intelligent Design]]'' (2004), written with [[Barbara Forrest]].<ref>{{Cite journal |last=Raff |first=Rudolf A. |date=2004 |title=The creationist Hydra grows a new head—a review of Unintelligent design by Mark Perakh and Creationism's Trojan horse by Barbara Forrest and Paul R. Gross' |url=https://dx.doi.org/10.1111/j.1525-142X.2004.04036.x |journal=Evolution & Development |volume=6 |issue=4 |pages=289–291 |doi=10.1111/j.1525-142X.2004.04036.x |via=EBSCOhost|url-access=subscription }}</ref>

Gross earned his [[Bachelor of Arts|A.B.]] in [[zoology]] and his Ph.D. in general [[physiology]] from the [[University of Pennsylvania]].<ref name=":0" /> He has taught at the [[Massachusetts Institute of Technology]], [[New York University]], [[Brown University]], and the [[University of Rochester]].<ref name=":0" /> From 1978 to 1988, he was Director and President of the [[Marine Biological Laboratory]] at [[Woods Hole, Massachusetts]].<ref name=":0" />

==Bibliography==
* (with [[Norman Levitt]]) ''[[Higher Superstition: The Academic Left and Its Quarrels With Science]]''. (Baltimore: Johns Hopkins University Press, 1994). {{ISBN|0-8018-5707-4}}
* ''Politicizing Science Education,'' Thomas B. Fordham Foundation, April 2000.
* "Berlinski Vanquishes Pseudoscience—Again," ''Commentary,'' December 16, 2002.
* "Intelligent Design and That Vast Right-Wing Conspiracy," ''Science Insights,'' September 2003.
* ''[[Creationism's Trojan Horse]]''. [[Oxford University Press]], 2004. {{ISBN|0-19-515742-7}}
* "Neo-creationist Tactics Show troubling Evolution," ''Science & Theology News,'' October 14, 2005.
* "Science Standards: We Can't afford to Go Light," ''National Review Online,'' November 16, 2005.
